title: Finance: Budgeting, Procurement, Contracts, and Revenue Recognition Guidance (2028)
author: Avery Chen
summary: Consolidated guidance covering Redwood Inference's budgeting and forecasting cadence, contract lifecycle and legal intake process, procurement procedures and thresholds, and high-level revenue recognition and billing policy considerations for 2026-2028.
body:
Purpose:
This document provides consolidated, operational guidance for finance, legal, procurement, and product stakeholders on budgeting and forecasting cadence, contract intake and approvals, procurement procedures and thresholds, and revenue recognition and billing practices. It is intended for use by finance business partners, legal counsel, procurement leads, accounting, and business owners responsible for P&L ownership.

Scope:
Applies to all Redwood Inference entities, revenue lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private), and cross-functional purchases or contracts initiated by product, engineering, sales, or GTM teams. Does NOT replace statutory accounting policies; for technical accounting determinations contact Accounting and External Audit.

1) Budgeting and Forecasting (operational guidance)
Overview:
- Annual Budget is prepared on a fiscal-year basis. The finance team issues the budget template in October for the following fiscal year; final approvals occur by December 15.
- Quarterly Forecasts are required for rolling 12-month forecasts and must be submitted two weeks before the monthly FP&A review.
- Drivers-based modeling: product revenue is modeled by product lines (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) with volume, ASPs, churn, and unit economics parameters (cost per token, GPU hours).
Key timelines and owners:
1. October 01 - Budget kickoff (FP&A)
2. November 15 - Department drafts due (Finance business partner)
3. December 01 - Executive review (CFO/CEO)
4. December 15 - Board-submitted budget (final)
5. Monthly - Forecast rebase (business owners)
SLA for submissions: department owners must submit templates by stated deadline; missed deadlines will trigger escalations to Finance VP.

Budget structure and required artifacts:
- P&L by department and product line (revenue, COGS, opex categories)
- CapEx schedule with asset-class, expected life, and procurement request ID
- Headcount plan with role, cost center, compensation band, and hire quarter
- Risk register: top 5 upside and downside scenarios and mitigation actions

Acceptance criteria for budget changes mid-year:
- Changes > 10% of department OPEX or > $250k must be accompanied by a variance rationale, updated forecast, and FP&A sign-off.
- Headcount increases outside hiring freeze require People Ops approval and CFO concurrence.

2) Contracts & Legal Process (intake to signature)
Contract intake workflow:
1. Initiation: Business owner completes the standard Contract Intake Form (Confluence link and Jira intake ticket). Include scope, term, auto-renewal, termination rights, PII/processing requirements, and estimated spending.
2. Legal review: Legal triages ticket within 2 business days for standard SaaS/Service agreements. Complex/custom terms routed to Senior Counsel with SLA of 5 business days.
3. Procurement/Finance review: For vendor agreements with > $50k annual spend, Procurement performs vendor risk checklist and Finance provides budget confirmation.
4. Signature: Authorized signatory list. Electronic signature via DocuSign is preferred.

Authorization matrix (examples):
- Individual contributor to $10k - Business owner sign-off
- Manager to $50k - Department head + Finance BP
- $50k to $250k - Director + Procurement + Finance VP
- > $250k - CFO approval + Legal counsel

Contract requirements checklist (minimum):
- Scope of work / deliverables
- Term and renewal terms; auto-renew details
- Pricing, payment terms, any pass-through costs
- Data protection and security obligations (if processing customer data)
- IP ownership & licensing
- Indemnity and limitation of liability
- Termination and transition assistance
- Confidentiality and audit rights

Contract playbook notes:
- Use the company-approved master services agreement (MSA) or vendor template where available. Any deviations > 3 clauses require Legal and Finance sign-off.
- Do not accept unilateral auto-renewal clauses longer than 12 months without Executive approval.

3) Procurement Procedures (POs, thresholds, vendor onboarding)
Procurement thresholds and approval flow:
- <$5k: Decentralized purchasing permitted using corporate card. Track via monthly Pcard reconciliation.
- $5k-$50k: Purchase Order (PO) required. Department head approval.
- $50k-$250k: PO + Procurement lead approval + Vendor risk assessment.
- >$250k: Competitive RFP (preferred), Procurement Director sign-off, and CFO approval for non-recurring purchases.

Vendor onboarding steps:
1. Complete Vendor Intake Form (W-9 / W-8 collection for tax)
2. Procurement completes vendor due diligence (financial health, sanctions screen, security posture)
3. Legal negotiates contract terms aligned to approved risk tolerance
4. Finance creates vendor record and assigns GL mapping

PO creation and matching:
- All POs must include cost center, GL code, expected delivery date, and contract reference
- Three-way match: PO, invoice, goods/services acceptance required for payments > $50k
- Blanket POs: permitted for recurring cloud and license spend; must be reconciled monthly and include termination clause

Expedited procurement:
- For mission-critical spend required to avoid customer-impacting outage, Procurement may issue an emergency PO with post-facto approvals documented within 5 business days. Emergency purchases must still be reviewed by Finance and Legal within 10 business days.

4) Revenue Recognition and Billing Policies (high-level guidance)
Principles and segregation of duties:
- Revenue recognition follows ASC 606 principles. Technical accounting judgments are handled by Accounting in conjunction with External Audit.
- Billing operations managed by Billing team; revenue accounting is owned by Accounting.

Common product patterns and recognition guidance (summary):
- Hosted API (usage-based): Recognize revenue over time as usage occurs. Deferred revenue recorded for prepayments/committed credits and amortized as usage is delivered.
- Dedicated (capacity/reserved): Fixed monthly/annual fee for reserved capacity recognized ratably over the contract term; variable overage recognized as incurred.
- Private deployments (license + services): License element evaluated for separability; implementation services recognized over time as performed.

Billing terms and invoicing cadence:
- Standard customers: Net-30 from invoice date. Hosted API customers billed monthly in arrears with detailed usage report attached.
- Enterprise: Contract-specified milestones or monthly/quarterly invoices per agreement. Billing team issues invoices within 5 business days of period close.
- Prepaid/committed plans: Recognize deferred revenue liability on receipt; amortize to revenue as delivered or when usage occurs.

Credit, collections, and disputes:
- Standard credit checks for new ARR > $50k annually. Sales must complete credit packet and procure POs where required.
- Collections cadence: 30/60/90-day follow-ups with escalation to Sales and Legal at 60 days. For amounts > $100k past due, apply hold on provisioning and notify Customer Success.
- Dispute process: customers submit billing disputes within 45 days. Billing team logs dispute, with Finance and Customer Success investigating and resolving within 15 business days.

Revenue reporting and close controls:
- Monthly close checklist includes reconciliation of billing system to general ledger, deferred revenue rollforward, and contract amendment review.
- Required supporting artifacts: executed contracts, billing reports, usage logs, and any credit/adjustment memos.

Appendix A - Example approval table
Threshold | Required Approvals | Notes
<$5k | Business owner | Corporate card allowed
$5k-$50k | Dept head + Finance BP | PO required
$50k-$250k | Director + Procurement + Finance VP | Vendor risk assessment
> $250k | CFO + Legal | RFP recommended

Appendix B - Quick checklist for sales and AMs when closing deals
- Attach executed contract to the opportunity and upload to Legal intake
- Confirm billing cadence and payment terms in the contract
- For committed spend, confirm prepayment schedule with Finance
- For any discounting greater than 15%, obtain Finance pricing approval

Governance and escalation:
- Finance, Procurement, and Legal meet weekly for active procurement and contract escalations
- Material policy exceptions (> $500k or non-standard legal indemnity) require an Exception Request form and Executive Committee approval

Questions and contacts:
- Budgeting/Forecast questions: FP&A (fpandateam@redwoodinference.internal)
- Procurement and vendor onboarding: procurement@redwoodinference.internal
- Contract intake and legal review: legal-intake@redwoodinference.internal
- Revenue recognition and billing: accounting@redwoodinference.internal
